about.title: Guadalupe Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Guadalupe is small enough that a death is felt on every block. With a population of 7,318, the city sits at the western edge of Santa Barbara County where Rt 166 passes through, and news travels quickly along Guadalupe Street and W Main Street. In 2025, public records show 8 injury collisions and 14 people hurt here, and no traffic deaths, a year local families can be grateful for. But wrongful death claims in Guadalupe do not come only from the road. A fall at work, defective equipment, a medical error, or a highway crash on Rt 166 can each leave a family without someone they depended on. California law gives a spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a civil claim, and it sets a two-year clock from the date of death. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Guadalupe families with an independent attorney who works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Guadalupe Families Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Not Everyone Has the Right to File
items.desc: California limits who can bring a wrongful death claim. A spouse or domestic partner and children come first, and certain dependents or heirs may qualify if there is no surviving spouse or child.

items.title: The Clock Starts on the Date of Death
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death to file a civil claim. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, the window to give notice is much shorter, so waiting can cost you the right to act.

items.title: The Law Recognizes More Than Bills
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs and the financial support the person would have provided. They can also include the loss of love, companionship, and guidance, which the law treats as real harm.

items.question: There were no traffic deaths in Guadalupe in 2025. Do wrongful death cases still happen here?
items.answer: Yes. The 2025 record of zero traffic deaths is good news for Guadalupe, but wrongful death claims are not limited to crashes on Guadalupe Street or Rt 166. Deaths tied to farm and warehouse work, medical care, unsafe property, or defective products can all support a civil claim. An independent attorney can review the specific circumstances and tell you whether the facts fit.

items.question: The person responsible is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action and does not depend on a criminal conviction. The two cases can move at the same time, and the two-year filing deadline keeps running regardless of what happens in criminal court. Talking with an attorney early helps protect your family's timeline.
